cuts.raw_narration: In a sunlit hospital room, a young boy named Gon sits upright in bed, one arm in a sling and a bandage across his forehead, as the tall lavender-haired examiner Satotz holds out a small blue card with a red double-X logo — the Hunter License. Satotz tells him that what matters is not the way you become a hunter, but what you do, and that Gon must decide for himself when he is ready to use it. Gon takes the card, turns it in his fingers, and breaks into a quiet, happy smile.

Later, in the arena where the final matches are being fought, Killua — a silver-haired boy — steps up for his match, only for the opponent to peel away the disguise: long black hair, chalk-pale skin, huge lifeless dark eyes. It is Killua's older brother, Illumi, in disguise. Killua's mouth trembles and sweat runs down his chin as he stares up at the towering figure, while Kurapika and Leorio watch in tense silence.

With a blank, oppressive calm, Illumi delivers his verdict: Killua was not born to be a hunter, he was born for one purpose — to be an assassin. The screen dissolves into a hypnotic spiral and Killua sees himself as a small child, alone under a single beam of light, shrinking beneath Illumi's towering shadow.

Pressed to name a single thing he actually wants, Killua looks down, his face crumpling, and finally says it out loud: he wants to be friends with Gon. He is sick of killing people. He just wants to be Gon's friend and have fun. Kurapika and Leorio watch, visibly shaken; Illumi's huge dark eyes stare back at him, completely empty.

Illumi tilts his head, raises a finger as if a small puzzle has just clicked into place, and calmly concludes that in that case he will simply kill Gon — assassins have no use for friends. A dark purple aura swells around him and Killua freezes rigid inside the same suffocating shadow.

Cornered by Illumi's threat — one step and Gon dies — Killua's mouth falls open in a ragged gasp and he chokes out that Illumi wins, he admits defeat. Illumi's face relaxes into a bright smile and he claps his hands together, then leans in, pats Killua on the shoulder, and drops the twist — he lied. He was never actually going to kill Gon. It was only a test.

Still standing over him with one hand resting on his head, Illumi delivers the verdict Killua just proved for him: he is simply not qualified to make friends. Not that he needs any. Killua does not answer. His enormous blue eyes go glassy and hollow, the light draining out of them as something inside him quietly gives up.

Later, after Killua has silently walked over and killed the recovering fighter Bodoro — getting himself disqualified — Gon shoves open the assembly hall's tall red doors and appears in the doorway, arm still in its sling, bandage still across his forehead, eyes burning. He walks straight past the other applicants and stops directly in front of Illumi.

Face to face with the man who broke his best friend, Gon glares up at Illumi's blank pale face with wide, furious eyes and demands that he apologize to Killua. Illumi looks down without a flicker of expression. Hisoka smirks quietly from the benches, Netero and the examiners watch in silence, Kurapika and Leorio sit frozen. Gon does not move, does not look away — a small boy in a sling standing up to an assassin, holding the demand.
